title: org-lsp configuration
description: The options of the org-lsp server, in its shared configuration file. See docs/configuration.md.

agendaFiles.description: Files, directories and glob patterns (`*`, `?`, `**`) the agenda is built from. `~/` is the home directory, and a directory stands for the Org files directly in it. When empty, the agenda is built from the Org files under the workspace folders (hidden directories, `node_modules` and `target` left out), or else from the Org files that are open. (`org-agenda-files`)

todoKeywords.description: The TODO sequence, written like Org's `#+TODO:` line. `|` separates the states that count as done; without it the last keyword is the only done state. `TODO(t)` gives a keyword a key for fast selection, and `WAIT(w@/!)` makes it log a note (`@`) or the time (`!`) on entering and leaving it. A file's own `#+TODO:` lines take precedence. (`org-todo-keywords`)

logDone.description: Write `CLOSED:` with the time when an entry is done, and with `note` ask for a note too. (`org-log-done`)

logRepeat.description: Record when a repeating entry is done and moves to its next date. (`org-log-repeat`)

logIntoDrawer.description: Put state changes and notes into a drawer: `true` for `LOGBOOK`, or the name of a drawer. (`org-log-into-drawer`)

tagsColumn.description: Where tags are aligned after a change to a headline. Negative: they end at that column. (`org-tags-column`)

useTagInheritance.description: Which tags entries inherit from their parents and from `#+FILETAGS:`: `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of tags, or a regexp (Emacs syntax) tags must match. Inherited tags count in tag searches and show in the agenda. (`org-use-tag-inheritance`)

tagsExcludeFromInheritance.description: Tags never inherited, when `useTagInheritance` is `true` or a regexp. (`org-tags-exclude-from-inheritance`)

usePropertyInheritance.description: Which properties an entry without them takes from its parents, the file's property drawer and `#+PROPERTY:` lines, in property searches (`OWNER="alice"`): `true` for all, `false` for none, a list of names, or a regexp (Emacs syntax). `CATEGORY` and `ARCHIVE` are always inherited. (`org-use-property-inheritance`)

clockIntoDrawer.description: Where `CLOCK:` lines go: `true` for the drawer of `logIntoDrawer` (`LOGBOOK` when that is not a name), the name of a drawer, or `false` for the entry itself. (`org-clock-into-drawer`)

clockOutRemoveZeroTimeClocks.description: Clocking out after less than a minute removes the `CLOCK:` line. (`org-clock-out-remove-zero-time-clocks`)

clockOutWhenDone.description: Marking the clocked entry done stops the clock. (`org-clock-out-when-done`)

completeTagsAlwaysOfferAllAgendaTags.description: Completing a tag offers the tags of every agenda file, after those of the file. Off, only the file's own. (`org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags`)

todoRepeatToState.description: The state a repeating entry returns to when it is done: a keyword, or `true` for the state it had. (`org-todo-repeat-to-state`)

priorityDefault.description: The priority of an entry without a cookie. A file's `#+PRIORITIES:` line takes precedence over the three priority options. (`org-priority-default`)

priorityStartCycleWithDefault.description: Raising or lowering the priority of an entry that has none starts at the default. (`org-priority-start-cycle-with-default`)

timestampRoundingMinutes.description: The step in which the minutes of a timestamp change (the second number of Org's option). (`org-time-stamp-rounding-minutes`)

readDatePreferFuture.description: A date typed without a year or month is the next one to come. With `time`, a time that has passed today is tomorrow's. (`org-read-date-prefer-future`)

readDateForceCompatibleDates.description: A typed year is kept within 1970 to 2037. (`org-read-date-force-compatible-dates`)

files.description: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths

maxLevel.description: The headlines up to this level

regexp.description: The headlines that match this regular expression

todo.description: The headlines with this TODO keyword

refileTargets.description: Where entries can be refiled to. Each entry has `files`: `current` (the entry's own file), `agenda`, a path or a list of paths; and one of `level`, `maxLevel`, `tag`, `todo`, `regexp` (the Rust `regex` crate's syntax) or `all` (true), which says which headlines there are targets. (`org-refile-targets`)

refileUseOutlinePath.description: Name targets by their outline path (`Projects/Alpha/`). The three names start the path with the file, and offer the file itself, for its top level. (`org-refile-use-outline-path`)

reverseNoteOrder.description: A refiled entry goes first under its target, not last. (`org-reverse-note-order`)

archiveLocation.description: Where archived subtrees go: a file, `::`, and a headline under which they go (they go to the end of the file without one). `%s` is the name of the file the subtree is in; an empty file part is that file. `datetree/` as the headline files them under year, month and day, by when they were closed. An `ARCHIVE` property of the entry or a parent, or a `#+ARCHIVE:` line, says otherwise. (`org-archive-location`)

archiveReversedOrder.description: An archived subtree goes first under its archive headline, not last. (`org-archive-reversed-order`)

archiveMarkDone.description: Mark archived entries done: `true` for the first done keyword, or the keyword to use. (`org-archive-mark-done`)

archiveSubtreeAddInheritedTags.description: Give an archived subtree the tags it inherited: always, never, or when it stays in its file. (`org-archive-subtree-add-inherited-tags`)

archiveSaveContextInfo.description: What an archived entry keeps as `ARCHIVE_…` properties: `time`, `file`, `olpath` (its outline path), `category`, `todo`, `itags` (inherited tags), `ltags` (its own tags) and `olid` (its parent's ID). (`org-archive-save-context-info`)

archiveSiblingHeading.description: The headline of the sibling `org.archive.sibling` archives under. (`org-archive-sibling-heading`)

archiveFileHeaderFormat.description: What a new archive file starts with; `%s` is the path of the file the subtree came from. (`org-archive-file-header-format`)

archiveDefaultCommand.description: What `org.archive.default` does: archive the subtree, archive it under its sibling, or tag it. (`org-archive-default-command`)

key.description: The keys that pick the template

prepend.description: First under the target, not last

target.description: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; or `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path

type.description: An Org entry (the default), or plain text

captureTemplates.description: Capture templates. Each has a `key`, a `description`, a `type` (`entry`, the default, or `plain`), a `target` and a `template` (text, or a list of lines), and may have `prepend`, `emptyLines`, `emptyLinesBefore`, `emptyLinesAfter` and `immediateFinish`. The target is a list: `file` and a path; `file+headline`, a path and a headline; or `file+olp`, a path and the headlines of an outline path. An empty path is `defaultNotesFile`, and without a target the entry goes at the end of `defaultNotesFile`. A template with only a key and a description groups the templates whose keys start with its key. (`org-capture-templates`)

orgDirectory.description: Where the relative paths of capture targets are. (`org-directory`)

defaultNotesFile.description: The target of a capture template whose file is empty. (`org-default-notes-file`)

linkDescriptive.description: Show a link as its description (or its target, when it has none) and hide the rest: the brackets, and the target of a link with a description. The text is marked `hidden` in the highlighting, and editors that can conceal text conceal it. (`org-link-descriptive`)

hideEmphasisMarkers.description: Hide the markers around `*bold*`, `/italic/`, `_underline_`, `+strike-through+`, `=verbatim=` and `~code~`, as for links. (`org-hide-emphasis-markers`)

autoSave.description: Save the files a command changes other than the one it was run in: an entry's file changed from the agenda, the target of a capture or of a refile. The editor saves them once it has made the change. Off, they are left with unsaved changes, as Emacs leaves them.

cycleSeparatorLines.description: With at least this many blank lines after a subtree, the last one stays outside its fold. Negative: all of them stay outside. `0`: none does. (`org-cycle-separator-lines`)

adaptIndentation.description: Indent the lines of an entry past its headline's stars: `true` for all of them, `"headline-data"` for the planning line, drawers and clock lines right below the headline. Applies to new lines, to re-indenting (range formatting) and to what commands write. (`org-adapt-indentation`)

startupIndented.description: Show files indented by level without changing them (`org-indent-mode`): the text under a headline lines up with its title, and leading stars are hidden. `#+STARTUP: indent` and `noindent` decide for a file. It turns `adaptIndentation` off in such files, unless that is `"headline-data"`. Editors that can show it: Neovim, and VS Code (not on wrapped lines). (`org-startup-indented`)

hideLeadingStars.description: Hide all the stars of a headline but the last; they keep their place. `#+STARTUP: hidestars` and `showstars` decide for a file. (`org-hide-leading-stars`)

srcPreserveIndentation.description: Leave the code of source blocks as it is indented when re-indenting. (`org-src-preserve-indentation`)

editSrcContentIndentation.description: How far code is indented past its source block when re-indenting. (`org-edit-src-content-indentation`)

span.description: How much time the agenda shows. (`org-agenda-span`)

startOnWeekday.description: The day a week or fortnight starts on; `false` starts it today. (`org-agenda-start-on-weekday`)

deadlineWarningDays.description: How many days before a deadline it shows up. (`org-deadline-warning-days`)

scheduledDelayDays.description: How many days after its date a scheduled entry shows up. (`org-scheduled-delay-days`)

scheduledPastDays.description: How many days a scheduled entry that is not done keeps showing up. (`org-scheduled-past-days`)

deadlinePastDays.description: How many days a missed deadline keeps showing up. (`org-deadline-past-days`)

skipScheduledIfDone.description: Leave out scheduled entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done`)

skipDeadlineIfDone.description: Leave out deadlines of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-deadline-if-done`)

skipTimestampIfDone.description: Leave out timestamps of entries that are done. (`org-agenda-skip-timestamp-if-done`)

showFutureRepeats.description: Show the future dates of repeating entries: all of them, none, or only the next. (`org-agenda-show-future-repeats`)

tagsColumn.description: Where tags are aligned in the agenda. Org's own default follows the window width, which a server does not know. (`org-agenda-tags-column`)

daily.description: Draw the grid in a one-day agenda. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

weekly.description: Draw the grid for every day. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

requireTimed.description: Draw the grid only on days with an entry that has a time. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

removeMatch.description: Leave out grid lines at a time an entry already has. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

times.description: The times of the grid lines, as `800` for 8:00. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

trailer.description: What follows a time that has no end time. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

line.description: The text of a grid line. (`org-agenda-time-grid`)

now.description: The text of the line for the current time. (`org-agenda-current-time-string`)

showCurrentTimeInGrid.description: Show the current time in the grid. (`org-agenda-show-current-time-in-grid`)

weekendDays.description: The days drawn as the weekend (0 is Sunday). (`org-agenda-weekend-days`)

startWithLogMode.description: Start the agenda in log mode, which shows what was closed and clocked each day (`l` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-log-mode`)

startWithClockreportMode.description: Start the agenda with the clock report under it (`R` toggles it). (`org-agenda-start-with-clockreport-mode`)

startWithArchivesMode.description: Start the agenda with entries in archived trees (`trees`; `v a` toggles it), or those and the files the agenda files archive to (`files`; `v A`). (`org-agenda-start-with-archives-mode`)

logModeItems.description: What log mode shows: `closed` entries, `clock` lines and `state` changes. (`org-agenda-log-mode-items`)

blockSeparator.description: What goes between the blocks of a block agenda: one character repeated across 79 columns, a longer text as it is, or `false` for nothing. In a block's `settings`, the separator above that block. (`org-agenda-block-separator`)

compactBlocks.description: Leave out the separators between blocks and the header over agenda blocks. (`org-agenda-compact-blocks`)

hideEmptyBlocks.description: Leave out the blocks of a block agenda that show no entries. Not in Org.

startDay.description: The day the agenda starts from, as the date prompt reads it: `-1d`, `+2d`, `2026-10-01`. (`org-agenda-start-day`)

blocks.description: Views shown one after the other

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

match.description: For todo, keywords; for tags, a match string

settings.description: Agenda options for this block: span, startDay…

header.description: Replaces the view's header; empty for none

key.description: The keys that pick the command in the agenda menu

match.description: For todo, keywords (NEXT|WAIT); for tags, a match string (work-home, PRIORITY="A")

settings.description: Agenda options for this command: span, startDay…

customCommands.description: Commands of the agenda menu. Each has a `key` and a `description`, and either a `type` (`agenda`, `alltodo`, `todo`, `tags` or `tags-todo`) with a `match` (keywords such as `NEXT|WAIT` for `todo`, a match string such as `work-home` or `PRIORITY="A"` for `tags`), or `blocks`, a list of such views shown one after the other. `header` replaces a view's header (empty: none), and `settings` holds agenda options for the command or a block (`span`, `startDay`…). A command with only a key and a description groups the commands whose keys start with its key. (`org-agenda-custom-commands`)
